prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2017 manifesto sets out a bold, unapologetic programme to complete a real Brexit, restore democratic sovereignty, control immigration, revive left‑behind communities, and put British citizens first in law, welfare, public services and national security.

Brexit and sovereignty
- “Guard dogs of Brexit” with six tests: restore full UK lawmaking supremacy; end free movement and take full border control; reclaim our 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone and fisheries; leave the Single Market and Customs Union; pay no “divorce bill” and recover UK assets; finish by end‑2019.
- Repeal the 1972 European Communities Act immediately; withdraw from the CFP and the 1964 London Convention; land fish in Britain; rebuild coastal economies; bring back the blue passport.
- Be WTO‑ready; seek global FTAs; walk away from bad EU terms.

Sound finances and lower bills
- Fund priorities from savings: end EU payments, cut foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrap HS2, reform the Barnett Formula. No tax rises.
- Cut the cost of living: remove VAT and green levies from domestic energy; abolish the TV licence; remove VAT on hot takeaways and sanitary products.
- Fairer taxes: raise the personal allowance to £13,500 and the 40% threshold to £55,000; lift IHT threshold to £500,000 (aim to abolish); flexible state pension window with option for women at 60; crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

Jobs, business and housing
- Back small firms: 20% business rates cut for premises under £50k RV; enforce prompt payment; open public procurement; no quarterly tax returns.
- British jobs first: require advertising to UK workers; lawful preference for under‑25 British applicants; protect workers’ rights; curb exploitative zero‑hours.
- Build up to 100,000 high‑quality factory‑built modular homes a year on brownfield via a new HDC; owner‑occupier only; resale to HDC at cost+inflation; release dormant public land.
- Coastal Enterprise Zones with 50% rates relief; revive boatbuilding and fishing.

NHS and social care
- Extra £11bn per year by 2021/22; integrate health and social care; licence and hold managers accountable; end PFI; scrap hospital parking charges; restore nurse bursaries; expand medical/nurse training with NHS service ties; streamline GP re‑entry; tougher eligibility for overseas users.
- Mental health: +£500m a year; 28‑day max waits; school counselling nationwide; oppose drug legalisation.

Older and disabled people
- Keep triple lock and universal pensioner benefits; +£2bn a year for social care; dignity code; protect home‑care choice; reform failing PIP/WCA; boost carers’ support.

Immigration and integration
- Balanced net migration to zero over five years: Australian‑style points plus permits; five‑year moratorium on low‑skilled migration; £30k salary floor for skilled; seasonal visas; no amnesty; five years’ contributions before benefits/non‑urgent NHS; attitude test on British values.
- One law for all: disband sharia councils; ban niqab/burqa in public places; zero tolerance of FGM, forced marriage, honour crime; firm school standards against Islamism.

Law, order and borders
- 20,000 more police, 7,000 more prison officers, 4,000 more Border Force; restore stop‑and‑search; tougher prisons; deport foreign criminals; opt out of the European Arrest Warrant; UK Bill of Rights; leave ECHR jurisdiction.

Defence and foreign policy
- Genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus £1bn a year; +20,000 personnel; fix procurement; Veterans’ Administration, housing and guaranteed jobs; avoid reckless wars; strong NATO/Five Eyes and US ties; “trade not aid” (aid to 0.2% GNI); commission a hospital ship.

Education and youth
- Grammar school in every town; strengthen technical/vocational routes; scrap unnecessary degrees; abolish tuition fees for STEM (and medical with service ties); restore maintenance grants; practical employability in curriculum.

Transport, environment, farming, energy
- Scrap HS2 and Heathrow third runway; back regional airports; end tolls; protect diesel drivers while accelerating EV charging.
- New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; brownfield first; cleaner seas.
- UK Single Farm Payment capped and focused on real farmers; support organic/hill farms; ban live exports; CCTV in abattoirs; clear slaughter labelling; tougher cruelty sentences.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave Paris/ETS; secure, affordable energy mix including shale (not in AONBs); cut commercial energy costs.

Real democracy and localism
- Abolish the House of Lords; create an English Parliament; halve the Commons and adopt proportional representation; binding citizen‑initiated referenda; tighten postal voting; empower councils and keep Council Tax low.
